title: A novel model of appendicitis and appendectomy to investigate inflammatory bowel disease
author: Cheluvappa
materials: 50 ml of sterile Phosphate Buffered Saline (PBS)
Sterile saline (Sodium Chloride Injections BP 0.9% tubes)
(5) Prepare surgical area observing sterile conditions meticulously:

steps.title: Prepare mice for surgery
steps.instruction: Use male BALB/c mice, 5 weeks old. One day before surgery shave a circumscribed area on the left abdomen, weigh each mouse, and place an identification mark on the tail.

steps.title: Set up sterile surgical field
steps.instruction: Wrap each P1000 pipette with a sterile plastic sheet, cover the bench with sterile plastic sheet and tape the corners, wear sterile gloves, load autoclaved instruments onto the sheet using a no‑touch method, load rubber bands, and pour povidone‑iodine onto a sterile tray.

substeps.instruction: Cover bench with sterile sheet and tape corners

steps.title: Anesthetize mice with ketamine/xylazine
steps.instruction: Prepare anesthetic stock containing ketamine 100 mg kg⁻¹ and xylazine 5 mg kg⁻¹ (Sigma‑Aldrich K1884, X1251). Inject intraperitoneally 0.1 ml of this stock per 20 g mouse weight.

steps.title: Pre‑operative mouse preparation
steps.instruction: Fix the mouse to the surgical platform by taping its limbs, moisten the eyes with a drop of sterile saline, wipe the abdomen with ethanol, apply povidone‑iodine to the shaved left side, cover the mouse with a sterile drape and cut a hole over the surgical site.

substeps.instruction: Cover with sterile drape and make opening

steps.title: Perform left‑side laparotomy
steps.instruction: Make a ~1 cm incision on the left abdomen using fine forceps to lift skin and peritoneum, keeping the field sterile.

steps.title: Expose and keep caecum moist
steps.instruction: Mobilise the caecum onto the surface with blunt curved forceps and frequently moisten it with sterile PBS.

steps.title: Identify target lymphoid patch
steps.instruction: Locate the 2–4 white caecal lymphoid patches; select the largest patch for manipulation.

steps.title: Create obstructed appendiceal pouch
steps.instruction: Load a sterile rubber band onto a beveled pipette tip with fine forceps. Aspirate the selected lymphoid patch (including a small amount of adjacent colonic tissue) with firm suction in a circular motion for 10 seconds, then slowly unload the band onto the neck of the newly formed pouch. Return the bowel to the cavity with curved forceps and dispense 1 ml PBS into the peritoneal cavity to keep it moist.

substeps.instruction: Load rubber band onto pipette tip
Aspirate lymphoid patch with suction for 10 s

steps.title: Close abdomen and immediate care
steps.instruction: Suture the abdominal wall and skin in layers, inject 1 ml normal saline subcutaneously at the scruff of the neck, and place the mouse on its side with cage mates to prevent hypothermia.

substeps.instruction: Place mouse on side with cage mates

steps.title: Sham surgery control
steps.instruction: Perform an identical laparotomy and manipulation without continuous band obstruction; instead place a sterile rubber band in the peritoneal cavity as a foreign‑body control, then close as described above.

steps.title: Randomize mice into groups
steps.instruction: Allocate each mouse to either the appendicitis (AA) group or the sham surgery (SS) group; other permutations (appendicitis‑only or appendectomy‑only) are excluded.

steps.title: Post‑operative monitoring
steps.instruction: Check recovery at 1 hour for full awakening, then monitor daily for one week, recording observations in the postoperative table.

steps.title: Day‑7 appendectomy or second sham
steps.instruction: Seven days after the initial operation, perform appendectomy on AA mice by gently separating adhesions, ligating, and excising the inflamed area distal to the ligature. Perform a second sham surgery on SS mice using the same steps but without ligation.

steps.title: Harvest distal colon at timepoints
steps.instruction: At 3, 14, or 28 days post‑appendectomy, euthanise the mice, remove the distal colon while excluding the rectum and a 1 cm segment from the anus.

steps.title: Flush colon and preserve in TRIzol
steps.instruction: Flush the harvested colon segment with normal saline to remove fecal contents, immediately place 50–75 mg of tissue in 600 µl TRIzol® reagent (Invitrogen 15596‑026), snap‑freeze in liquid nitrogen, and store at –80 °C until analysis.

steps.title: RNA extraction from colon tissue
steps.instruction: Add chloroform, centrifuge, precipitate RNA with isopropanol, wash the pellet with 75 % ethanol, air‑dry, and re‑suspend in nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: Measure RNA concentration and purity
steps.instruction: Determine RNA concentration and purity using a Nanodrop ND‑1000; accept samples with OD260/280 ≥ 1.8 and OD260/230 ≥ 1.8.

steps.title: Assess RNA integrity
steps.instruction: Run RNA on an Agilent Bioanalyzer 2100 and confirm that the RNA integrity number (RIN) is consistently above 7.
